interest: Vanity Fair caricature, Seattle burlesques and a New York mock trial strained diplomacy over Hirohito's image in the 1930s.
keywords: American Friends of the Chinese People
overview: This file consists of a ten-page Department of State 'List of Papers' (purport and docket list) for decimal file 894.001 Hirohito (Emperor of Japan), recording incoming and outgoing diplomatic correspondence, memoranda, consular despatches, and cross-reference sheets between April 1930 and May 1938. The docket entries document annual ceremonial exchanges of birthday greetings between the President of the United States and the Emperor, as well as diplomatic fallout from assassination attempts on Hirohito and Japanese officials, such as the 1932 Sakuradamon Incident and the Hongkew Park bombing in Shanghai. A major portion of the file indexes extensive diplomatic protests and Department discussions concerning perceived insults to the Emperor in American periodicals—notably the August 1935 Vanity Fair cartoon, a burlesque performance in Seattle, a planned 1936 mock trial by the American Friends of the Chinese People in New York, and subsequent articles in Life and Ken magazines. Additionally, the file indexes detailed reporting on Japanese domestic constitutional controversies, specifically the denunciation of Dr. Tatsukichi Minobe's institutional theory of the Emperor, alongside public diplomacy efforts including the 1936 goodwill delegation of the Veterans of Foreign Wars to Japan.

subfiles.summary: This ten-page State Department List of Papers compiles entries for decimal file 894.001 (Hirohito, Emperor of Japan) spanning April 1930 to May 1938. It details annual ceremonial communications including presidential birthday greetings and imperial replies, as well as diplomatic repercussions following the 1932 Sakuradamon assassination attempt and the Hongkew Park bombing in Shanghai. The register tracks diplomatic controversies surrounding American press portrayals of the Emperor, notably the August 1935 Vanity Fair cartoon, a burlesque performance in Seattle, an attempted mock trial by the American Friends of the Chinese People in New York, and subsequent articles in Life and Ken. In addition, the entries index reports on Japanese internal political controversies including Dr. Tatsukichi Minobe's 'emperor-as-an-organ' constitutional theory, goodwill exchanges involving the Veterans of Foreign Wars, and celebrations of the imperial birthday in Peru.
